ai.description: *Nanorana liebigii* is a robust frog (6–9 cm) with olive-brown skin and dark mottling. It features a broad, flattened head, distinct tympanum, and heavily tuberculate skin on the dorsum and flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana liebigii* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, black-tipped nuptial spines on the chest and forelimbs of males, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana liebigii* inhabits high-altitude Himalayan streams and rocky torrents, typically found between 1,500 and 4,000 meters within temperate forests and alpine meadows.
ai.behavior: The Sikkim Paa frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by remaining motionless to blend into rocky, high-altitude stream environments.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana liebigii* breeds in mountain streams from May to August, laying clutches of 100–300 large, unpigmented eggs attached to the underside of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana liebigii* occurs across the Himalayas in India, spanning states like Sikkim, West Bengal, and Himachal Pradesh at elevations between 1,500 and 3,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Sikkim Paa Frog produces a series of low-pitched, pulsed "gurgling" or "croaking" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing mountain streams in the Himalayas.
